outcome: The core problem (existence of resolution of singularities for varieties of dimension ≥ 4 over fields of positive characteristic) remains open. The only substantive AI-related development in the window is an exploratory 2026 paper by Gergely Bérczi using DeepMind's AlphaEvolve to evolve candidate termination-invariant ("ranking function") constructions for a simplified toy model of the canonical blow-up process in dimension 4, characteristic 3; the paper states two conjectures, not a proof, and does not resolve any case of the actual geometric problem. A separate, unrelated 798-page arXiv preprint (2608.20066, Aug 2026) claims a full resolution in all dimensions and characteristics, but shows strong hallmarks of being an AI-generated, non-peer-reviewed, likely nonsensical text (invented unexplained terminology such as 'total-Hasse activity packets', 'paid quotients', 'displayed parents', 'terminal truth'; the listed author has a Princeton 'Complex Infrastructure Systems' affiliation, not a mathematics one; no expert digestion, citation, or discussion of it exists anywhere).

ai.basis_quote: "the mathematical conclusions, conjectures, and counterexamples presented here arise from independent mathematical analysis" ... "this is a report ... describing a possible way to use AlphaEvolve as an experimental engine ... rather than as a finished mathematical theory" — AlphaEvolve (using gemini-2.5-pro / gemini-3-pro) evolved three explicit candidate ranking functions inside a fixed evaluation harness (a toy canonical blow-up simulator with human-designed features and benchmarks); the author then analyzed the outputs and formulated the paper's two formal conjectures about a discretized five-component lexicographic ranking function satisfying a bounded-delay descent criterion.
ai.disclosed_cost: Eleven experiments reported, with individual run durations ranging from 3 to 22 days (e.g. a first focused benchmark run of 26 hours and a discretization experiment of 24 hours).

disputes.summary: arXiv:2608.20066 (Chenxiao Tian, Aug 2026, 798 pages, 'Frobenius-Hasse Towers and Exceptional-History Descent') explicitly claims a full canonical strong embedded resolution and principalization construction over any perfect field of characteristic p>0 — i.e., a complete solution to the stated open problem. No expert digestion, review, citation, or discussion of this preprint could be found anywhere (no MathOverflow, blog, or forum commentary), it uses extensive invented terminology not found in the resolution-of-singularities literature ('total-Hasse activity packets', 'filtered coefficient cubes', 'semilinear Frobenius-Hasse sources', 'paid quotients', 'displayed parents', 'terminal truth', 'six-row defect calculus'), and the listed author's Princeton page (cis.princeton.edu) places them in a 'Complex Infrastructure Systems' lab, not a mathematics department, with no other mathematical publication record found. These are strong indicators of an AI-hallucinated or AI-generated preprint rather than genuine mathematics; it is treated here as uncredentialed noise rather than as a genuine claimed proof, and is not counted as 'claimed' status.

summary: The bullet concerns resolution of singularities in positive characteristic, open (as of Jan 2024) for varieties of dimension ≥ 4 over fields of characteristic p>0 (dimension ≤3 was already settled: surfaces by Abhyankar 1956, threefolds by Cossart–Piltant 2008–2009). Wikipedia's current article still states the higher-dimensional case as open, and I found no genuine proof or digested partial result advancing the general higher-dimensional problem in the window. The one substantive, verifiable AI-related development is Gergely Bérczi's Feb 2026 preprint (arXiv:2602.06553), which used DeepMind's AlphaEvolve (an LLM-driven evolutionary code-search system, built on Gemini models) to search for termination/ranking-function invariants in a deliberately simplified toy model of the canonical blow-up process (dimension 4, characteristic 3, monic purely inseparable leading term). This is honestly and explicitly framed by the author as exploratory: AlphaEvolve produced candidate ranking-function code within a human-built simulator and evaluation harness; the author independently analyzed the results, found a counterexample to an initial 'perfect' candidate, and formulated two conjectures about a five-component discretized ranking function. No proof of any case of the actual geometric resolution problem resulted — this is progress on a research programme (evolving ranking-function candidates as a heuristic-discovery tool) rather than a solved case, so status is `progress` and `ai_role` is `bound` (an AI system contributed to narrowing/exploring the landscape of a still-open problem, not to settling any part of it). Separately, I encountered a much more dramatic-looking claim: arXiv:2608.20066 (Aug 2026), a 798-page preprint by 'Chenxiao Tian' claiming to fully solve the stated problem in all dimensions and characteristics via a byzantine apparatus of invented terminology. I judge this very likely to be an AI-generated (hallucinated or LLM-authored) paper rather than genuine mathematics: the prose is dense with meaningless-sounding coined jargon uncorrelated with the literature, no expert has engaged with or cited it, and the listed Princeton affiliation is to an infrastructure-systems lab rather than mathematics, with no other mathematical track record found for this name. Because no human expert has validated (or even engaged with) this claim, and because its authorship/provenance itself is suspect, I do not count it as a `claimed` resolution — I record it only in `disputes` as a credibility flag rather than let it drive the status field, consistent with §6.1's requirement that even `claimed` status rest on a serious, engaged-with claim. I also checked the RIMS Kyoto Univ. 2024 publication on embedded resolution of surface singularities in arbitrary characteristic; this is an expository/summary account of an already-published 2020/2021 result (arXiv:2011.14443) with no AI involvement, and not new progress in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue arXiv:2608.20066 should be recorded as `claimed` with `ai_role` `generated`, since if genuine, it would fully resolve the conjecture and the writing style is consistent with an AI-generated proof attempt. I judge the evidence (invented terminology untethered to the literature, non-mathematical author affiliation, complete absence of any expert or community engagement even a year after typical circulation, and the sheer implausibility of a 798-page single-author solo resolution of a problem that has resisted the field for 60 years suddenly appearing with no preceding partial results from the same author) points toward this being unreliable noise rather than a genuine claim worth scoring, but I cannot rule out with certainty that it is a serious (if extremely dense) human-written attempt that simply hasn't been read yet.
what_would_settle_it: Any expert commentary, referee report, or citation addressing arXiv:2608.20066's validity; confirmation or denial from the named author regarding their identity/field and whether an AI system was used to draft the manuscript; or a retraction/withdrawal notice on arXiv. For the Bérczi AlphaEvolve line of work, a follow-up paper proving the conjectures for the toy model, or extending results to genuine (non-toy) resolution invariants, would move the status toward `partial`.
